The test image shows a corn leaf with extensive damage: numerous small, scattered tan/white spots and lesions across the surface, mixed with brown/reddish-brown discoloration and remaining green areas. The leaf is severely affected with coalescing damage.

This is a **leaf** disease. Let me check reference images from my top candidates one at a time.
SCLB reference shows rectangular tan lesions on a mostly green leaf - early stage, not matching the severe scattered pattern. Let me check Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows discrete spindle-shaped lesions, not matching. Let me check Holcus_Spot.
Holcus spot shows individual small spots, not the severe scattered pattern. Let me check Eyespot.
Eyespot shows scattered small spots but not the severe coalescing pattern. Let me check Southern_Rust.
Southern rust shows orange pustules, not matching. Let me check Common_Rust.
Common rust shows raised dark pustules, not matching. Let me check Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight (advanced) and Northern_Leaf_Blight.

That's all 8 reference views used. The Eyespot reference (Corn_Disease_10.jpg) is the closest match to the test image. Both show numerous small, circular spots scattered across the leaf surface. The test image appears to be a severe/advanced case where the characteristic small round eyespot lesions have coalesced, causing extensive leaf blight with tan/white centers and brown discoloration between spots. The other candidates (SCLB, Anthracnose, Holcus, Southern Rust, Common Rust) showed distinctly different lesion patterns that don't match.
